mcpDescription: Let AI assistants analyze finalized captures and focus the waveform. Enable editing to manage markers, reports, saved results and analyzers, and create derived captures while preserving the original waveform. Saving a capture also preserves its analysis data.
mcpAllowAnnotations: Allow assistants to edit the analysis workspace
animationScaleHint: Length of the zoom and pan glide. 0 is instant, 1 is 100 ms, 3 is 300 ms.
clearLogsHint: Deletes every retained log file and starts a fresh one. Cannot be undone.
copyLogFilesHint: Puts the log files themselves on the clipboard so you can paste them straight into a report as attachments. Pasting the text instead would be unreadable at this size.
copyLogsHint: Copies the environment plus the tail of both logs as text, capped so it stays pasteable. Use the button above for anything you intend to attach.
diagCaptureHint: Samples held, the sample rate they were taken at, and the time span they cover.
diagDrawPathsHint: Waveform draws recorded since load and the most-used path. Only recorded in development builds.
diagFrameLoopHint: Whether the backend frame loop is wired for this session and has produced a frame yet. The loop owns the viewport while a capture is loaded.
diagMemoryHint: Memory used by the loaded capture against the configured capture memory limit.
gridLinesHint: Draw the time grid behind the waveform. Turn it off for a cleaner trace when reading values by eye.
logDefaultLevelHint: Verbosity for every module that has no level of its own, in both the webview and the backend log. Debug and trace stay in the webview buffer; only info and above reach the log file.
logModuleHint: Overrides the default level for one part of the app. A module you leave alone follows the default, so raise only the one you are chasing.
logPausedHint: Stop writing logs to disk. Turn it on only if you need the machine quiet; recording is bounded and on by default so the run that breaks is already captured.
logUsageHint: How much the retained log files take against the hard cap. Each launch gets its own file, capped in size, and the oldest are deleted.
matchChannelColorsHint: Draw digital and analog channels in the same colour.
panToTriggerHint: Move the view to the trigger when a capture arrives.
renameTabToSavedCaptureHint: Use the saved file name as the session tab title.
resetAllHint: Restores every option on this panel to its default value.
saveLogsHint: Writes the same bundle to a file you choose, for report trackers that want an attachment.
mcpSetupDescription: Let your agent inspect captures, analyze signals and place precise markers.
mcpDesktopRequired: Open the SigPilot desktop application to enable MCP.
mcpUnsupported: Desktop MCP is unavailable on this system.
mcpPersistenceHint: Settings are saved automatically. Keep SigPilot running while connected.
mcpAutoStartFailed: Automatic startup was requested but the service is off. Enable it again; if another SigPilot window owns MCP, disable it there first.
mcpBridgeMissing: The MCP component is missing. Reinstall the complete SigPilot package.
mcpMergeHint: This configuration contains only the HTTP address. Keep your existing servers; no API key is needed.
mcpCheckMeaning: The service check verifies SigPilot’s HTTP server. Confirm agent access through actual tool calls. Reload MCP after changing permissions or restarting SigPilot.
mcpTestPrompt: Use the sigpilot MCP tools to list open sessions and read their sample rate and sample count. If multiple captures are open, ask which one to use. If editing is enabled and the capture has at least 6 samples, add a timing marker named MCP test at sample 5 (5 μs at 1 MHz), then read it back to confirm the exact position.
mcpLocalOnly: The service listens only on 127.0.0.1. The agent’s MCP client must run on this computer; a cloud-hosted client needs a separate local relay.
mcpClaudeAvailability: Claude Desktop is officially available for macOS and Windows. On Linux, use a compatible MCP client with the JSON below.
mcpPermissionHint: Create markers, configure decoders and save analysis results.
mcpCommandHint: Run once in a terminal with the {{client}} CLI installed.
mcpInstallHint: Open Cursor's MCP installer and confirm the server in Cursor.
mcpInstallOpened: Open request sent. Confirm the installation in Cursor.
mcpNext_codex: Complete authorization after running the command. To sign in again, run codex mcp login sigpilot. Start a new session and check /mcp.
mcpNext_claude_code: Restart Claude Code, select sigpilot in /mcp and authenticate.
mcpNext_cursor: Confirm the installation, then use Cursor in Agent mode.
mcpNext_claude_desktop: Merge the configuration below into Claude Desktop's MCP settings, save and restart the client.
mcpNext_generic: Add this HTTP URL in your client and complete OAuth authorization. Streamable HTTP and OAuth support are required.
mcpVerifyHint: Paste the test task into your agent chat to confirm it can read the capture and call tools.
mcpOAuthHint: Approve the first connection in SigPilot’s AI / MCP panel. No API key is needed. Authorization survives restarts and can be revoked in advanced details.
mcpAuthorizationHint: Allow this client to use MCP tools. Editing and device capture follow the separate permissions above. The client supplies its name; check that this is the connection you just started.
mcpPortHint: Default: 10531 on every platform. An occupied port produces an error. After changing it, update the agent URL and authorize again.
mcpAllowCapture: Allow agents to capture from devices
mcpCapturePermissionHint: Start and stop bounded acquisitions in new tabs. An occupied device is never interrupted; you can stop recording from the desktop.
mcpCaptureStarted: Agent requested capture; preparing the device…
mcpCaptureBusy: A capture is already running. Stop it or wait for it to finish before starting another.
mcpCaptureVerifyHint: Ask your agent to capture from the Demo device, then inspect the new tab and returned results.
mcpCaptureTestPrompt: Use SigPilot MCP to list devices and read the Demo device capabilities. Start a 10 ms digital capture on D0–D3 at 1 MHz, with an 8 MiB buffer and a 10-second deadline. Poll until it finishes, then return its capture reference, actual sampling rate and sample count, and read the first few edges on D0.
